introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Further Mathematics 3 (0775), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2023. Time allowed: two and a half hours.**

Answer ALL questions. For your guidance the approximate mark allocation for parts of each question is indicated in brackets. Mathematical formulae and tables, published by the Board, and noiseless non-programmable electronic calculators are allowed. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage.
enonce_intro_markdown: A force $\mathbf{F}_1$ of magnitude $2\sqrt{29}\ \mathrm{N}$ acts along the line $\mathbf{r} = [(\mathbf{i}+\mathbf{k}) + \alpha(3\mathbf{i} - 2\mathbf{j} - 4\mathbf{k})]\ \mathrm{m}$.
incertitudes: Question 1 : le sujet ne dit pas dans quel sens agit F1 le long de la droite. Le sens des alpha croissants (F1 = 6i - 4j - 8k) est le seul compatible avec la résultante R donnée en (ii) ; il est justifié dans le corrigé. Le travail trouvé (116 J) en dépend.
Question 1 : la force F3 est lue « (-i + 4k) N » sur le scan (filigrane gênant) ; cette lecture est confirmée par R = 4i - 3j - 4k et par |G| = 3 racine de 13, tous deux retrouvés exactement.

Question 1 : le sujet ne donne pas de position pour F1 : on prend le point de la droite d'indice alpha = 0, c'est-à-dire i + k (le moment d'une force ne dépend pas du point de sa droite d'action choisi).

questions.enonce_markdown: Find the work done by $\mathbf{F}_1$ in displacing a particle from the point where $\alpha = 0$ to the point where $\alpha = 2$.
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Direction of the force.** The line has direction vector $\mathbf{d} = 3\mathbf{i} - 2\mathbf{j} - 4\mathbf{k}$, with $|\mathbf{d}| = \sqrt{9+4+16} = \sqrt{29}$. The force acts along the line with magnitude $2\sqrt{29}\ \mathrm{N}$. Taking it in the sense of increasing $\alpha$ (this is the sense that gives the resultant $\mathbf{R}$ of part (ii)):

$$\mathbf{F}_1 = 2\sqrt{29}\cdot\frac{\mathbf{d}}{\sqrt{29}} = 2\mathbf{d} = (6\mathbf{i} - 4\mathbf{j} - 8\mathbf{k})\ \mathrm{N}$$

**Displacement.** The particle goes from $\alpha = 0$ to $\alpha = 2$, so

$$\mathbf{s} = \mathbf{r}(2) - \mathbf{r}(0) = 2\mathbf{d} = (6\mathbf{i} - 4\mathbf{j} - 8\mathbf{k})\ \mathrm{m}$$

**Work done** is the scalar product of the force and the displacement:

$$W = \mathbf{F}_1\cdot\mathbf{s} = 6\times 6 + (-4)(-4) + (-8)(-8) = 36 + 16 + 64 = 116\ \mathrm{J}$$

(Check: the force and the displacement are parallel, so $W = |\mathbf{F}_1||\mathbf{s}| = 2\sqrt{29}\times 2\sqrt{29} = 116\ \mathrm{J}$.)

**$W = 116\ \mathrm{J}$.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
The forces $\mathbf{F}_2$ and $\mathbf{F}_3$ act at points with position vectors $\mathbf{r}_2$ and $\mathbf{r}_3$ respectively, where

$$\mathbf{F}_2 = (-\mathbf{i} + \mathbf{j})\ \mathrm{N},\quad \mathbf{r}_2 = (\mathbf{j} + \mathbf{k})\ \mathrm{m}$$

$$\mathbf{F}_3 = (-\mathbf{i} + 4\mathbf{k})\ \mathrm{N},\quad \mathbf{r}_3 = (\mathbf{i} + \mathbf{j} + \mathbf{k})\ \mathrm{m}$$

The system of forces $\mathbf{F}_1$, $\mathbf{F}_2$ and $\mathbf{F}_3$ is equivalent to a single force $\mathbf{R}$, acting through the origin $O$, together with a couple $\mathbf{G}$. Show that $\mathbf{R} = (4\mathbf{i} - 3\mathbf{j} - 4\mathbf{k})\ \mathrm{N}$.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The single force at $O$ equivalent to the system is the vector sum of the forces:

$$\mathbf{R} = \mathbf{F}_1 + \mathbf{F}_2 + \mathbf{F}_3$$

With $\mathbf{F}_1 = 6\mathbf{i} - 4\mathbf{j} - 8\mathbf{k}$ (from part (i)):

$$\mathbf{R} = (6 - 1 - 1)\mathbf{i} + (-4 + 1 + 0)\mathbf{j} + (-8 + 0 + 4)\mathbf{k} = 4\mathbf{i} - 3\mathbf{j} - 4\mathbf{k}$$

So $\mathbf{R} = (4\mathbf{i} - 3\mathbf{j} - 4\mathbf{k})\ \mathrm{N}$, as required.

questions.enonce_markdown: The forces $\mathbf{F}_1$, $\mathbf{F}_2$ and $\mathbf{F}_3$ are the same as in parts (i) and (ii): $\mathbf{F}_2 = (-\mathbf{i} + \mathbf{j})\ \mathrm{N}$ acts at $\mathbf{r}_2 = (\mathbf{j} + \mathbf{k})\ \mathrm{m}$, $\mathbf{F}_3 = (-\mathbf{i} + 4\mathbf{k})\ \mathrm{N}$ acts at $\mathbf{r}_3 = (\mathbf{i} + \mathbf{j} + \mathbf{k})\ \mathrm{m}$, and the system is equivalent to a single force $\mathbf{R}$ acting through the origin $O$ together with a couple $\mathbf{G}$. Show that the magnitude of the couple $\mathbf{G}$ is $3\sqrt{13}\ \mathrm{N\,m}$.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The couple $\mathbf{G}$ is the sum of the moments of the three forces about $O$:

$$\mathbf{G} = \mathbf{r}_1\times\mathbf{F}_1 + \mathbf{r}_2\times\mathbf{F}_2 + \mathbf{r}_3\times\mathbf{F}_3$$

For $\mathbf{F}_1$ we may use any point of its line of action, for instance $\mathbf{r}_1 = \mathbf{i} + \mathbf{k}$ (the point $\alpha = 0$).

**Moment of $\mathbf{F}_1$:**

$$\mathbf{r}_1\times\mathbf{F}_1 = \begin{vmatrix}\mathbf{i}&\mathbf{j}&\mathbf{k}\\1&0&1\\6&-4&-8\end{vmatrix} = (0\cdot(-8) - 1\cdot(-4))\mathbf{i} - (1\cdot(-8) - 1\cdot 6)\mathbf{j} + (1\cdot(-4) - 0\cdot 6)\mathbf{k} = 4\mathbf{i} + 14\mathbf{j} - 4\mathbf{k}$$

**Moment of $\mathbf{F}_2$:**

$$\mathbf{r}_2\times\mathbf{F}_2 = \begin{vmatrix}\mathbf{i}&\mathbf{j}&\mathbf{k}\\0&1&1\\-1&1&0\end{vmatrix} = (0 - 1)\mathbf{i} - (0 + 1)\mathbf{j} + (0 + 1)\mathbf{k} = -\mathbf{i} - \mathbf{j} + \mathbf{k}$$

**Moment of $\mathbf{F}_3$:**

$$\mathbf{r}_3\times\mathbf{F}_3 = \begin{vmatrix}\mathbf{i}&\mathbf{j}&\mathbf{k}\\1&1&1\\-1&0&4\end{vmatrix} = (4 - 0)\mathbf{i} - (4 + 1)\mathbf{j} + (0 + 1)\mathbf{k} = 4\mathbf{i} - 5\mathbf{j} + \mathbf{k}$$

**Sum:**

$$\mathbf{G} = (4 - 1 + 4)\mathbf{i} + (14 - 1 - 5)\mathbf{j} + (-4 + 1 + 1)\mathbf{k} = 7\mathbf{i} + 8\mathbf{j} - 2\mathbf{k}\ \mathrm{N\,m}$$

**Magnitude:**

$$|\mathbf{G}| = \sqrt{7^2 + 8^2 + (-2)^2} = \sqrt{49 + 64 + 4} = \sqrt{117} = \sqrt{9\times 13} = 3\sqrt{13}\ \mathrm{N\,m}$$

as required.
